observed_evidence.ref: git parent 31b2f0c8c1fe13e2e3962c6cdabb9e2f61b57c53 of second claim commit 22c0bc98e32641057658ba1f74b042f45840eb2a
observed_evidence.finding: The first claim is present at the second claim's parent ref. Therefore the duplicate is not explained by eventual visibility of the first claim; the coordination key itself permits semantic duplication when workers choose different research_id values.

problem: Current Trigger-6 create-only coordination keys the mutex by <research_id>/<claim_target>.json. research_id is worker-selected/provenance-like and is not a canonical semantic objective identity. Two workers can therefore create different paths for the same target workpackage, evidence stage and materially overlapping objective even when the earlier claim is already visible.

architecture_delta.name: TRIGGER6_CANONICAL_OBJECTIVE_KEY/v1
architecture_delta.principle: Separate provenance identity from coordination identity.
canonical_mutex_key_inputs: target_project/workpackage/module set in canonical sorted form
external source pin or upstream claim id when the objective is source-specific
experiment/discriminator id when the objective is experiment-specific
architecture_delta.research_id_role: Provenance and lineage only; stored inside the claim but excluded from mutex-path uniqueness.
normalization_requirements: versioned objective taxonomy instead of free-text-only similarity
fail closed when an objective cannot be normalized with sufficient specificity
architecture_delta.compatibility: Existing per-research-id claims remain historical provenance. New objective claims should be additive and authoritative for duplicate-work exclusion; no second truth/state authority is introduced.

required_negative_tests: Two different research_id values with same WP803 targets, E1 stage and same normalized objective class produce the same objective_key and second create fails.
Same research_id with E1 vs E2 produces different objective_key.
Same WP but different external source pins produce different source-specific objective_key when both are legitimately distinct.
Architecture snapshot change produces a distinct review objective only when marked as explicit stale re-review rather than silently duplicating the original.
Free-text wording changes do not bypass a canonical objective taxonomy key.
Ambiguous objective normalization fails closed rather than minting a fresh mutex path.
counterhypothesis: A central semantic objective registry may add coordination overhead and false-positive blocking between legitimately distinct research angles. The fix should therefore use typed objective classes and explicit source/discriminator pins, not fuzzy text similarity as authority.
expected_benefit: Prevent duplicate expensive Trigger-6 research while preserving independent objectives, reducing source-reading/tool/token duplication and avoiding false independent-replication counts.
expected_runtime_effect: No Frankenstein runtime/model token impact; coordination-only development overhead.
